title: Only 7% Pass This Harvard Entrance Exam
summary: Read the evidence, compare the numbers and make decisions that stand up to scrutiny.

landing.intro:
Read the clues. Make the connections.
Put your thinking to the test.

about.body:
Read the evidence, compare the numbers and make decisions that stand up to scrutiny.

Use the facts, rules and quantities in each question. No specialist university knowledge is required, and there is no speed score. Each checkpoint reflects the topic just completed. The final result combines your answers, with an optional review of the questions you missed.

This independent entertainment challenge is inspired by academic reasoning. It is not an official Harvard admissions test, an assessment of academic potential or a prediction of admission.

steps: Read the clues and choose one answer.
See your topic profile at each checkpoint and continue to a new challenge.
Reveal your overall result, then optionally review the answers you missed.

about.disclaimer: Independent entertainment challenge. Not an official Harvard admissions test and not affiliated with any university.

next.tagline: A small calculation can change the best choice.
A convincing story still needs the right evidence.
The wording can be as important as the numbers.
Now look at what the figures actually show.
Which choice fits the goal that was actually set?
A few rules can narrow the options sharply.
Every attractive option gives something up.
Put the numbers and the evidence together.
The last cases combine rules, quantities and judgement.

score.passed: You passed the Harvard entrance challenge!

harvard-s1q1.question: Every approved proposal has a budget. This proposal is approved. What must it have?

harvard-s1q2.question: A meeting needs both a room and a speaker. The room is confirmed, but no speaker is confirmed. What is true?

harvard-s1q3.question: A rule says a permit is required to enter. Lee has a permit. What does that tell us?

harvard-s1q4.question: All urgent messages are flagged. This message is not flagged. Under the rule, what follows?

harvard-s1q5.question: Three reports are due in order: A before B, and B before C. Which must come first?

harvard-s1q6.question: A team can choose exactly one location: north, south or east. North and east are unavailable. Which remains?

harvard-s1q7.question: A label says “at least 12 seats”. Which seat count would break that description?

harvard-s2q1.question: A team completes 24 tasks in 6 hours at a constant rate. How many tasks per hour?

harvard-s2q2.question: A project has 200 credits. It spends 35% of them. How many credits remain?

harvard-s2q3.question: Three equal payments total 84 credits. What is one payment?

harvard-s2q4.question: A price rises from 50 credits to 60 credits. What is the percentage increase?

harvard-s2q5.question: A plan costs 8 credits per week plus a one-time fee of 12 credits. What is the total for 4 weeks?

harvard-s2q6.question: Six identical machines finish a job in 4 hours. With equal constant rates, how long would three machines take?

harvard-s2q7.question: A bag has 18 blue and 12 red tokens. What fraction of all tokens is red?

harvard-s3q1.question: Sales rose after a new sign appeared. What does that fact alone establish?

answers.a2: The sign caused the entire rise
answers.a4: The rise followed the sign change

harvard-s3q2.question: A survey asks only people leaving a cinema whether they enjoy films. What is its main limit?

answers.a2: The sample may overrepresent film fans
answers.a4: The answers must all be false

harvard-s3q3.question: Which observation disproves “Every delivery arrived before noon”?

harvard-s3q4.question: Two teams try different tools but also receive different training. Why is comparison difficult?

answers.a3: Training could also affect the outcome

harvard-s3q5.question: Which best tests whether a new queue system reduces waiting time?

answers.a1: Compare waiting times in similar conditions with and without it
answers.a2: Count the letters in its name
answers.a4: Ask its designer if it looks good

harvard-s3q6.question: A report names its source, date and sample size. What does this primarily help a reader do?

answers.a1: Check how the claim was produced

harvard-s3q7.question: A claim rests on one customer review. What would most strengthen a broad conclusion about customers?

answers.a2: The same review in a larger font

harvard-s4q1.question: A report calls a result “tentative”. How should it be treated?

harvard-s4q3.question: A proposal is “feasible” if it is…

harvard-s4q4.question: “Some proposals were accepted.” What is guaranteed?

answers.a4: At least one proposal was accepted

harvard-s4q5.question: Which sentence states a cause rather than just a sequence?

harvard-s4q6.question: A decision is “reversible”. What does that mean?

harvard-s4q7.question: Which is the clearest summary of “The cheaper plan saves money but takes longer”?

answers.a1: It costs more but is faster
answers.a3: It trades lower cost for more time
answers.a4: Both plans take the same time

harvard-s5q1.question: Weekly visitors are 20, 30 and 40. What is the mean?

harvard-s5q2.question: Team A completes 18 of 20 tasks; Team B completes 24 of 30. Which has the higher completion rate?

harvard-s5q3.question: A chart shows 45 visits on Monday and 60 on Tuesday. How many more visits were on Tuesday?

harvard-s5q4.question: A group has 80 members. Of them, 60 answered a survey. What percentage responded?

harvard-s5q5.question: The values are 2, 3, 3, 4 and 18. What is the median?

harvard-s5q6.question: A result says “40 of 50 respondents agreed”. Which statement adds an unsupported claim?

harvard-s5q7.question: A rate changes from 10% to 15%. What is the increase in percentage points?

harvard-s6q1.question: Choose the cheapest plan that finishes within 3 days. A costs 40 and takes 4 days; B costs 60 and takes 3; C costs 80 and takes 2. Which wins?

harvard-s6q2.question: A task must be finished before any others can begin. What makes it a priority?

harvard-s6q3.question: A team wants fewer errors. Which measure most directly tracks that goal?

harvard-s6q4.question: Only one option is affordable and meets every required feature. Which is justified by those rules?

harvard-s6q5.question: You can run a small reversible trial before a costly uncertain decision. What is the main benefit?

harvard-s6q6.question: Two plans give the same stated benefit. A costs 30 credits; B costs 45. If cost is the only other criterion, which is better?

answers.a4: The more expensive one by definition

harvard-s6q7.question: A decision depends on whether demand exceeds 100 units. Which missing fact matters most?

harvard-s7q1.question: A pass requires both a photo and a signature. Jo supplies a photo only. What is true?

answers.a3: The requirements are not yet met

harvard-s7q2.question: Choose two different projects costing at most 10 credits together. A costs 7, B costs 4 and C costs 3. Which pair works?

answers.a4: A and C, or B and C

harvard-s7q3.question: A workshop holds no more than 18 people. Four groups of 5 arrive. How many people exceed capacity?

harvard-s7q4.question: X must happen after Y and before Z. Which order satisfies both rules?

harvard-s7q5.question: A room is available only after 14:00. Which start time is allowed?

harvard-s7q6.question: Exactly one of two switches must be on. Switch A is on. What must be true of B?

harvard-s7q7.question: A rule requires a score of at least 75. Which pair both meet it?

harvard-s8q1.question: You spend an hour on Plan A instead of Plan B. What is the opportunity cost?

answers.a2: The benefit you give up from Plan B
answers.a4: The cost of both plans combined

harvard-s8q2.question: A route takes 20 minutes and costs 8 credits; another takes 35 minutes and costs 3. What does the first route buy?

answers.a2: 15 minutes saved at no extra cost
answers.a4: More time and a lower cost

harvard-s8q3.question: A team has already paid a non-refundable fee. What should guide whether to continue now?

answers.a1: The fee alone, regardless of outcomes
answers.a3: The future benefits and future costs
answers.a4: The original name of the plan

harvard-s8q4.question: Plan A is faster; Plan B is cheaper. Neither goal is ranked. What is needed to choose between them?

answers.a1: The number of letters in each name
answers.a2: A guarantee that speed never matters
answers.a4: The relative importance of time and cost

harvard-s8q5.question: A backup costs 5 credits and prevents a stated 50-credit loss if a failure occurs. What extra fact is needed to compare expected costs?

answers.a2: The day the plan was named

harvard-s8q6.question: Two offers have identical total cost, speed and quality. Only their labels differ. Based on those criteria, what follows?

answers.a1: The shorter label must be better
answers.a4: Neither is better on the stated criteria

harvard-s8q7.question: A trial can be expanded later if it works. Which feature makes that possible?

answers.a1: The plan allows a staged commitment
answers.a4: The full budget is spent immediately

harvard-s9q1.question: One trial has 30 successes in 40 attempts. A second trial has 21 in 30. Which has the higher success rate?

harvard-s9q2.question: A plan needs 120 credits. Funding provides 45 and 55 credits. What is the shortfall?

harvard-s9q3.question: A survey has 200 responses, 60% positive. How many are positive?

harvard-s9q4.question: Two equal-sized groups average 60 and 80 points. What is their combined mean?

harvard-s9q5.question: A target is 90 tasks. The team completes 28, 31 and 26. How many more are needed?

harvard-s9q6.question: An estimate is revised from 400 to 360 units. What percentage decrease is that?

harvard-s9q7.question: Demand is 70 units. Each full pack contains 12 units, and only whole packs can be ordered. How many packs are needed?

harvard-s10q1.question: A choice must cost at most 50 and score at least 8. A is 45/7; B is 55/9; C is 50/8. Which qualifies?

harvard-s10q2.question: A shop earns 6 credits per item after variable costs. Fixed costs are 48 credits. How many items cover those costs exactly?

harvard-s10q3.question: A study changes both the price and the packaging, then sales rise. Which conclusion is warranted?

answers.a3: Their separate effects are not established

harvard-s10q4.question: A task takes 2 hours, then a second takes 3 hours. They cannot overlap. Starting at 09:30, when do they finish?

harvard-s10q5.question: A report says the evidence is “consistent with” a theory. What is the careful reading?

answers.a1: The theory is proven beyond all doubt
answers.a2: The evidence fits, without proving it uniquely

harvard-s10q6.question: Plan A costs 20 now and 5 per use. Plan B costs 8 per use with no initial fee. At 10 uses, which costs less?

harvard-s10q7.question: A recommendation requires reliable demand data and an affordable plan. The plan is affordable; the demand data are missing. What should the conclusion be?

answers.a1: The recommendation is not yet established
